question.text: A nucleus with mass number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>242</mn></math> and binding energy per nucleon as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math> breaks into two fragment each with mass number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>121</mn></math>. If each fragment nucleus has binding energy per nucleon as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the total gain in binding energy is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Binding energy is given by E=∆mc2

where ∆m is the mass defect.

The energy per nucleon of the nucleus having mass number 242 is 7.6 MeV.

The initial binding energy is,

BE=242×7.6 MeV

The energy per nucleon of the nucleus with mass number 121 is 8.1 MeV.

Therefore, binding energy is

BE'=2121×8.1 MeV

The gain in the binding energy is 

BE'-BE = (8.1 – 7.6) × 242 MeV=121 MeV

= 121 MeV
